QUOTE: `MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(member)` expand to `private_##member` by default, and to plain `member` only when `MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS` is defined. ... Inside those files, `MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(x)` resolves to the real `x`. ... an application that writes `ctx->state` gets a compile error, because the member is really named `private_state`.
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer explains that code defining the macro sees plain names while ordinary consumers of the public headers see `private_`-renamed members.
